root_cause.text: KVM’s x86 MMU page-fault handling in `mmu_set_spte()` created an MMIO SPTE for `is_noslot_pfn(pfn)` before zapping an existing shadow-present SPTE at the same GFN, leaving a stale present mapping in `arch/x86/kvm/mmu/mmu.c` instead of replacing it safely.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `is_noslot_pfn(pfn)`/`mark_mmio_spte()` path from before the `is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep)` handling to after it, and adds a TLB flush after marking MMIO; the CVE text says KVM “will install the MMIO SPTE without first zapping the shadow-present SPTE,” and the warning triggers in `mark_mmio_spte()` on `is_shadow_present_pte(*sptep)`.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: KVM’s x86 MMU page-fault handling in `mmu_set_spte()` created an MMIO SPTE for `is_noslot_pfn(pfn)` before zapping an existing shadow-present SPTE at the same GFN, leaving a stale present mapping in `arch/x86/kvm/mmu/mmu.c` instead of replacing it safely.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the early noslot-PFN MMIO SPTE path so `mmu_set_spte()` handles those mappings through the normal SPTE flow.
intent_record.what: The code block that special-cased `is_noslot_pfn(pfn)` was removed from `mmu_set_spte()`. That block previously incremented `vcpu->stat.pf_mmio_spte_created`, called `mark_mmio_spte(vcpu, sptep, gfn, pte_access)`, and returned `RET_PF_EMULATE`.
intent_record.how: After this change, `mmu_set_spte()` no longer immediately converts noslot PFNs into MMIO SPTEs and exits at this point. The function will now continue into the later SPTE handling logic, changing how such PFNs are processed during page fault/SPTE installation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle no-slot PFNs by creating MMIO SPTEs and returning emulation instead of building normal mappings.
intent_record.what: An early return block was added in mmu_set_spte() that checks `unlikely(is_noslot_pfn(pfn))`; when true, it increments `vcpu->stat.pf_mmio_spte_created`, calls `mark_mmio_spte(vcpu, sptep, gfn, pte_access)`, conditionally flushes remote TLBs for the GFN and level, and returns `RET_PF_EMULATE` before the call to `make_spte()`.
intent_record.how: This changes runtime behavior so that PFNs that do not belong to a valid memory slot are treated as MMIO SPTEs instead of being passed through normal SPTE creation. It prevents invalid/no-slot PFNs from being mapped as regular memory, records the MMIO SPTE creation, and ensures stale TLB entries are flushed when needed.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets the root cause by removing the early is_noslot_pfn() MMIO SPTE creation path in mmu_set_spte(), which was leaving a stale shadow-present SPTE instead of replacing it safely.

The group directly concerns the same mmu_set_spte() no-slot PFN/MMIO SPTE path as the root cause. It changes handling of is_noslot_pfn(pfn), which is the code path involved in creating an MMIO SPTE and relates to the stale shadow-present mapping issue.

candidates.rationale: This early return path created an MMIO SPTE for no-slot PFNs before the code reached the normal shadow-present-SPTE handling that could zap an existing mapping at the same GFN, which is the core stale-mapping bug.
This statement installs the MMIO SPTE immediately on the no-slot PFN path, directly triggering the unsafe replacement behavior described in the root cause.
Returning immediately here prevents later logic from zapping the existing shadow-present SPTE, leaving the stale present mapping in place.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early branch diverts no-slot PFNs into an MMIO-SPTE path before the normal SPTE replacement/zap logic runs, which is the root cause of leaving a stale shadow-present mapping at the same GFN.
This statement installs the MMIO SPTE immediately on the no-slot PFN path, creating the replacement that can occur before an existing present SPTE is safely zapped.
This early return exits before the later shadow-present-SPTE handling can run, preventing the stale mapping from being removed.

Author: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>

    Now that it should be impossible to convert a valid SPTE to an MMIO SPTE,

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is the creation of an MMIO SPTE for `is_noslot_pfn(pfn)` before the code that handles overwriting/removing an existing shadow-present SPTE. In this commit, that logic is moved to the top of `mmu_set_spte()`: `if (unlikely(is_noslot_pfn(pfn))) { mark_mmio_spte(vcpu, sptep, gfn, pte_access); return RET_PF_EMULATE; }`. Because the MMIO case is handled directly in `mmu_set_spte()` before any of the shadow-present SPTE replacement logic, the stale-present-mapping condition described in the root cause is no longer present. The old helper `set_mmio_spte()` and the `if (set_mmio_spte(...)) return 0;` path were removed from `set_spte()`, and the later `if (unlikely(is_mmio_spte(*sptep))) ret = RET_PF_EMULATE;` check was also removed, showing the fix is already applied in this code.
